questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the equation of a hyperboloid of two sheets centered at $O$ is given by

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}-\frac{{z}^{2}}{{c}^{2}}=-1.
$$

Thus, our equation is a hyperboloid of two sheets with $a=b=c=1.$

Recall that the equation of an elliptic cylinder centered at $O$ is given by

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

Thus, our equation is an elliptic cylinder with $a=b=\sqrt{2}.$

Recall that the equation of a hyperbolic paraboloid centered at $O$ is given by

$$
z=\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}},
$$

and a hyperbolic paraboloid centered at $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ is given by

$$
z-{z}_{0}=\frac{(x-{x}_{0})^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(y-{y}_{0})^{2}}{{b}^{2}},
$$

Thus, our equation is a hyperbolic paraboloid with the following parameters:

$$
({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})=(1,-1,0),\,a=5,\,b=4.
$$

Recall that the equation of a hyperbolic cylinder, whose axis of symmetry is the $z$-axis, is given by

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

Thus, our equation is a hyperbolic cylinder with $a=3,\,b=4.$

Recall that the equation of a parabolic cylinder, whose axis is the $z$-axis, is given by

$$
{x}^{2}=4py.
$$

Thus, our equation is a parabolic cylinder with $p=2.$

$$
\frac{{z}^{2}}{{c}^{2}}=\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}.
$$

Thus, an elliptic cone centered at $O$ whose axis of symmetry is the $x$**-axis** is given by

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}=\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{{c}^{2}}.
$$

Therefore, our equation is an elliptic cone whose axis of symmetry is the $x$-axis and $a=1,\,b=c=2.$

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying Quadric Surfaces by Completing the Square
questions.worked_solution:
First, we complete the square in the $y$ term:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+3{y}^{2}+12y-z+13 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}+3({y}^{2}+4y)-z+13 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}+3[(y+2)^{2}-4]-z+13 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}+3(y+2)^{2}-12-z+13 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}+3(y+2)^{2}-z+1 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, by rearranging, we get the equation

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+3(y+2)^{2}-z+1 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}+3(y+2)^{2} & =z-1.\end{aligned}
$$

This is the equation of an elliptic paraboloid centered at $(0,-2,1).$

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying Quadric Surfaces by Completing the Square
questions.worked_solution:
First, we complete the square in the $x$ and $z$ terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}^{2}-4{z}^{2}-4x-y-16z-12 & =0 \\ 2({x}^{2}-2x)-4({z}^{2}+4z)-y-12 & =0 \\ 2[(x-1)^{2}-1]-4[(z+2)^{2}-4]-y-12 & =0 \\ 2(x-1)^{2}-2-4(z+2)^{2}+16-y-12 & =0 \\ 2(x-1)^{2}-4(z+2)^{2}-y+2 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, by rearranging, we get the equation

$$
\begin{aligned}2(x-1)^{2}-4(z+2)^{2}-y+2 & =0 \\ 2(x-1)^{2}-4(z+2)^{2} & =y-2\end{aligned}
$$

This is the equation of a hyperbolic paraboloid centered at $(1,2,-2).$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we complete the square in the $x$ term:

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}^{2}+{z}^{2}+2x+y & =0 \\ -({x}^{2}-2x)+{z}^{2}+y & =0 \\ -(x-1)^{2}+1+{z}^{2}+y & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, by rearranging, we get the equation

$$
\begin{aligned}-(x-1)^{2}+1+{z}^{2}+y & =0 \\ -(x-1)^{2}+{z}^{2} & =-y-1 \\ (x-1)^{2}-{z}^{2} & =y+1.\end{aligned}
$$

This is the equation of a hyperbolic paraboloid centered at $(1, -1, 0).$
